Before you brief

Practical questions.

How much does event styling cost in Australia?
Styling is usually quoted one of two ways: individual hire items priced per piece, or a styling package priced for the whole space. As a broad guide, a ceremony-only styling brief with an arbour, aisle pieces and a signing table commonly sits between $1,500 and $4,000; a full wedding or gala with backdrops, furniture, tables, lighting and setup more often runs $8,000 to $25,000 and beyond. Room size, ceiling height, install complexity and whether setup and pack-down are included move the number more than the individual props do.
What is the difference between an event stylist and an event planner?
A stylist is responsible for how the space looks and feels — the design direction, the furniture, the structures, the tabletop and the install. A planner is responsible for how the event runs — budget, suppliers, timeline and coordination on the day. Some businesses offer both, but they are separate scopes and usually separate fees. The Set Edit covers styling and hire; planning and coordination sit outside what a brief here is matched to.
What furniture do I need for a 100-person event?
For a seated dinner of 100, plan on ten round tables of ten or four to five long banquet tables, plus 100 chairs and a small number of service tables. For a cocktail event of 100, allow roughly eight to twelve cocktail tables, two to three lounge settings and seating for about 30 per cent of guests — people move, so you do not need a chair each. Add a gift or signing table, a cake or feature plinth, and a bar surface if the venue doesn't supply one.
How many cocktail tables do I need for 80 guests?
Six to ten is the usual range for 80 guests. Fewer than six and people have nowhere to put a glass; more than ten and the floor stops flowing. Mix heights if you can — a few low lounge settings alongside high cocktail tables gives guests somewhere to sit without turning the room into a seated dinner.
How far in advance should I book event hire and styling?
Six to twelve months for a wedding or a large corporate event, particularly between October and April when the calendar is tightest. Three to six months is workable for smaller milestone events. Statement pieces — large backdrops, custom structures, specific furniture ranges — are the first things to go, so if your design depends on one particular element, book earlier.
Does event hire include delivery and setup?
It varies, and it is the single most common source of budget surprise. Some hire is dry hire — you collect, install and return it yourself. Others quote delivery, install, styling and pack-down as a package. Bump-in and bump-out windows, venue access, stairs and after-midnight collection all affect the price. Always ask for delivery, setup and pack-down to be itemised separately in a quote.
What props do I need for an outdoor wedding?
Start with the structural pieces: an arbour or ceremony structure, seating, a signing table and signage. Then consider what the site does not provide — power for lighting, a level surface for furniture, weather cover, and a wet-weather alternative. Outdoor sites usually need more infrastructure and a longer install window than an indoor venue, so budget for the setup, not just the pieces.
Do you own the furniture and props shown on this site?
No. The Set Edit is a design-led inspiration and planning brand. Every image on the site illustrates a styling direction and a category of hire, not stock we hold. When you build a brief, it is passed to relevant local event styling and hire professionals who supply and install the work.
